News.title: Schools & roads to shut over safety fears as ‘large numbers’ to gather for funeral of Middlesbrough A66 crash victim
News.content:
SCHOOLS in Middlesbrough are set to close early tomorrow amid safety fears ahead of a funeral for one of the victims of the horror A66 crash.

Roads will also be shut off as “large numbers of people” are expected in North Yorkshire to pay tribute to Jakub Matusiak, 23.



He was one of five young men killed when their Volkswagen Passat hit a marked police car while going the wrong way down a dual carriageway.

Cole Worthy, 17, Theo Rae, 17, Makai Saddington, 18 and Michael Cahill, 23, also died following the fatal crash on the A66.



Jakub’s funeral will be held at the St John the Evangelist Church, with big crowds, motorbikes and quad bikes likely in the area tomorrow.

It is expected to be starkly different to the vigil held there for the two cops killed in the smash, PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.



Fury erupted as five motors were torched and plumes of smokes filled the air at a twisted tribute for Michael Cahill last week.

Kate Dearden MP, described the scenes as “absolutely horrendous” and urged cops to “get on” with their investigation into the crash.



Cahills’ mum had urged people to bring “bikes, jeeps, cars and quads” to give her son “the send off he deserves”.

And there are fears of a similar turnout at the service for Matusiak tomorrow, prompting locals schools to take urgent action.

At least four schools will shut, with South Bank Primary saying it would be closing at midday “to ensure the safety and wellbeing of our pupils”.



Writing on social media, headteacher Tammy Cooper said: A funeral is being held locally at St John’s church on Normanby Road that day.

“We are expecting large numbers of people in the area which will inevitably cause congestion and transport disruption in the area.

“This decision has been reached after careful consideration of the potential impact on the departure of pupils, staff and families.

“We recognise the inconvenience this may cause and thank our families for their understanding and co-operation.”

Ms Cooper said the school also recognises “some pupils may feel upset or anxious about the funeral taking place locally”.



Mark Robinson, principal of Outwood Academy, said the school would also close following discussions between local headteachers and the council.

Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council confirmed “a number of schools in the South Bank area will close earlier than usual on Friday afternoon”.

The local authority said: “The decision was made after careful consideration of the potential impact on home-to-school transport and the departure of pupils, staff and families at the end of the school day.

“Schools have worked with the local authority and transport providers to consider arrangements for pupils, including those who travel to and from specialist educational settings.

“We recognise that early closure may cause inconvenience for some parents and carers.



“We thank them for their understanding and co-operation.”

The A66 smash has sparked a wave of gang violence in Middlesbrough, with two hundred specialist cops being drafted in to restore order.

The fallout saw a gangland feud which had been bubbling up for months burst out into the open.

Sources say homes have been rammed for months as part of a tit-for-tat campaign involving rivals amid a gangland feud over “drugs and money“.

And, in an unrelated incident on Wednesday, a woman and seven-year-old girl were killed in a house fire.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Young Valentina Foster and her aunt Natalie McDonald, 34, tragically died in the blaze at 5.23am.

Local MP Andy McDonald previously said residents feel “trapped in their own homes” and don’t feel safe enough to go to the shops.

News.title: Life’s most unforgettable moment is getting married followed by birth of first child
News.content:
UNFORGETTABLE MOMENTS Life’s most unforgettable moment is getting married followed by birth of first child

LIFE’S most unforgettable moments include hearing your baby’s heartbeat for the first time, a dream holiday and falling in love, according to a new poll.

Getting married claimed the top spot (49 per cent), followed by the birth of a first child (47 per cent) and losing a loved one (45 per cent).



Other cherished memories to make the top 40 include getting a pet (21 per cent), seeing your favourite artist live (20 per cent) and achieving financial independence (20 per cent).

Purchasing a first car, landing a dream job and graduating from university also featured prominently in the poll of 2,000 people.



Overall, 57 per cent of the most unforgettable moments relate to family, with only four per cent stemming from work or careers.

Pip Deacon from John Lewis Money, which commissioned the research, said: “Whether moving into your first home, experiencing the chaos of a new puppy, or going on the holiday of a lifetime – it’s the memorable milestones that make life special.

LIFE’S TOP 40 MOST UNFORGETTABLE MOMENTS: Getting married The birth of your first child Losing a loved one Having children Buying a first home Passing your driving test Falling in love Meeting a life partner Losing a pet Getting engaged Going on your dream holiday Starting a first job A once‑in‑a‑lifetime trip Purchasing your first car Your child’s first day at school Leaving home for the first time Hearing your baby’s heartbeat for the first time Finding out you were pregnant Leaving school Retiring Graduating Bringing a pet home for the first time Seeing your favourite artist live Achieving a long‑term goal Achieving financial independence Landing your dream job Moving to a new country Getting into university Your child’s first performance at school Watching your favourite band for the first time Finding out your baby’s gender Winning a competition Getting a promotion Your child’s last day at school Purchasing your dream car Winning an award Watching your favourite team score a winning goal Meeting your favourite celebrity Quitting a job Starting a business

“No one looks back fondly on life admin or even work, aside from those four per cent in our survey, which is why we’re helping customers take care of the things they love – from pets and homes to cars and holidays – so they can focus on making lifelong memories.”

The research went on to find 97 per cent would like to relive their most unforgettable moments, with just under a quarter (24 per cent) wanting to do this at least weekly.

As many as nine in 10 think it’s important to preserve these memories, with millennials being the most sentimental – as 94 per cent agreed.



And 68 per cent believe thinking about their happiest moments help them out when they’re having a bad day.

Furthermore, 52 per cent like to preserve memories by looking through photo albums, and 37 per cent do this by scrolling through pictures on their camera roll.

Three in 10 save important letters and cards, and 19 per cent make memory boxes full of keepsakes like notes and train tickets.

And 56 per cent are excited to find out what their next milestone will be, with Gen Z being the most excitable with 85 per cent claiming this to be true, according to the stats by OnePoll.

Pip Deacon from John Lewis Money added: “It’s heartwarming to see how cherished people’s memories are, and how impactful they can be on a bad day.



“And with people already looking forward to making new memories, there will be plenty of exciting times ahead.”

News.title: Moment ‘stolen’ van seen hurtling ‘wrong way’ down A20 in police chase before being rammed by cops
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment a van was seen hurtling the “wrong way” down the A20 in a police chase before being rammed by cops.

Footage appears to show a white Citroen repeatedly swerving between lanes on the major A-road in Kent on Sunday.



The video, filmed by a passenger in a vehicle travelling on the opposite side of the road, shows the van hurtling along the eastbound carriageway with its hazard lights flashing.

Dozens of motorists scrambled to avoid a head-on collision as the vehicle motored down the A20.



The Citroën allegedly exited the dual carriageway by driving the wrong way up a slip road.

Officers then rammed the vehicle off the road in Bromley, south-east London, before arresting the driver.

Shocking images from the scene show the allegedly stolen vehicle suspended in the air, surrounded by shattered glass.

The van was stopped by police on Mottingham Road, Bromley, after it was pursued around 17 miles from Swanley into London.

At least eight police vehicles were pictured at the scene as cops swarmed the area.

Kent Police said the incident began after the van was allegedly taken from an address in Swanscombe.



It then travelled into London after failing to stop for officers in Swanley.

The pursuit ended on Mottingham Road at around 7.40pm on Sunday, August 30.

One Met officer suffered an injury to his hand during the incident and was taken to hospital.



He has since been discharged and no other serious injuries were reported.

Barney McGinley, 33, has been charged with causing serious injury by driving a vehicle dangerously, dangerous driving, driving whilst disqualified and no insurance.

He appeared before Croydon Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday where he was remanded in custody.

A spokesman for Kent Police said in an updated statement: “Kent Police was called at 2.55pm on Sunday to a report that a man had smashed a window and taken a van that did not belong to him from an address in Swanscombe.

“The owner of the property was known to him. At around 6.45pm Kent Police officers located the van in the London Road area of Swanley.



“It did not stop and travelled into London, where Metropolitan Police officers assisted in the detention of the driver after making tactical contact with the vehicle in Mottingham Road, Bromley.

“One Metropolitan Police officer suffered an injury to his hand during the incident and no other serious injuries were reported.”

It comes just days after two hero police officers were killed in a split-second horror when a car packed with five young men came racing the wrong way down the A66.

The VW Passat smashed head-on into their patrol car, killing PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The five men in the Passat also died in the devastating collision in Middlesbrough, as cops continue to investigate the moments leading to the fatal smash.



Days before this tragedy, five teenagers died in a separate but similar wrong-way motorway smash in Ireland.

News.title: Over 800 barrels of Guinness worth £205,000 stolen from depot as cops hunt two men
News.content:
STOUT-RAGEOUS Over 800 barrels of Guinness worth £205,000 stolen from depot as cops hunt two men

TWO trailers containing more than 800 barrels of Guinness have been stolen, as police issue an appeal for witnesses.

At around 7:45pm on Monday, August 31, a lorry was seen entering an industrial estate in Cheshire.



The same vehicle then connected to a trailer, before a second lorry followed closely behind into the Runcorn estate.

By 9:30pm, both trailers had been connected and taken away in the direction of Rainhill and Watkinson Way.



It was estimated the total value of all the items stolen is approximately £205,000.

The trailers are described as white Tri-Axle Curtain side trailers with GXO company branding on curtains and rear doors.



One of the men driving the truck was described as being white, having a short dark beard and wearing a beanie.

The second man was described as “wearing a cap”.

Police are now appealing for witnesses to come forward with any information about the thefts.

Detective Sergeant McClatchy said: “It is famously said that “Guinness is good for you”, but that is only the case when it has been bought and paid for.



“It is with this in mind that we have wasted no time in launching enquiries to identify those responsible for the theft of £115,000 worth of Guinness and the two trailers that housed the barrels – we will settle for nothing less than the full recovery of all the items stolen.

“As part of our investigation to fully establish what has occurred, we are now appealing to anyone who has any information in relation to the theft to please come forward and speak to officers.

“We would also ask any motorists who were driving in the area at the time of either of the incidents to please review any dashcam footage to see if you have captured anything that could aid our investigation.”

News.title: Teen boys charged after ‘vulnerable young woman and two girls under 16 raped’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

'RAPE' HORROR Teen boys charged after ‘vulnerable young woman and two girls under 16 raped’

TWO teenage boys have been charged after a vulnerable young woman and two girls under 16 were allegedly raped.

The alleged offences happened at addresses in North Somerset, western Somerset and in Cornwall, police said.

The teens, both from Somerset, were remanded into youth detention after appearing at Taunton Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday.



Avon and Somerset Police said the charges relate to a vulnerable young woman and two teenage girls, aged under 16.



A 17-year-old has been charged with three counts of rape of a girl aged under 16 and one count of non-fatal strangulation.

He was also charged with one count of assault by causing actual bodily harm.

A 16-year-old has also been charged with three counts of rape of a girl aged under 16 and one count of rape of a woman aged 16 or over.

He was also charged with one count of non-fatal strangulation and one count of assault causing bodily harm.

Neither boy can be named due to their age with police adding their “self-defined ethnicity is white British”.

They are being held in a youth detention centre pending a further hearing at Taunton Crown Court on September 25.

News.title: Girl, 12, killed by ‘drunk-driver’ while crossing road just days before her birthday as heartbroken family pay tribute
News.content:
'UNIMAGINABLE PAIN' Girl, 12, killed by ‘drunk-driver’ while crossing road just days before her birthday as heartbroken family pay tribute

A YOUNG girl has been mowed down and killed by a suspected drunk-driver as she crossed a road just days before her birthday.

Janessa Gonzalez, 12, was struck by a Ford Mustang at around 5.37pm on Monday in Terra Bella, California. She suffered major injuries and was rushed to hospital, but later died.



Cops have arrested Anthony Chavez-Valencia, 22, of nearby Porterville, on suspicion of driving under the influence.

Investigators believe alcohol may have been a factor in the crash, although the circumstances remain under investigation.



Janessa was just nine days away from turning 13 on September 10.

Instead of preparing for her birthday, her family are now preparing for her funeral.



Her devastated great-grandmother Eleanor Pina said: “It’s been awful without her. I can’t imagine having her one day, and the next day she is gone.”

Janessa was crossing Avenue 95 when she was hit near Terra Bella Elementary School.

This week, around 200 people gathered for a vigil as the community continues to mourn the youngster.

Her family describe her as a girl who could “light up a room” and said she was “bright, funny” and full of life.



She was the second oldest of six children and had a particularly sweet side.

Janessa loved babies and would carry her baby dolls around in her arms, caring for them as though they were real children.

Her family also described her as “a whole character” who was funny, loving, stubborn, sweet and always trying to help someone.



They said: “Once she started talking, she could talk your ear off.”

Janessa had already overcome huge challenges before her life was cut tragically short.

Her family said doctors had told her mum that she would never walk or talk. Janessa proved them wrong.

“She showed them, she fought harder than anyone could have imagined and did things they said she would never do,” they said.

They added: “She proved them wrong just by being Janessa.”



Now her brothers and sisters must face life without their sister.

Her family said they will miss “the sound of her voice, her smile, her personality, and simply having her here with us”.

Terra Bella Unified School District superintendent Nicolas Garcia said the tragedy had shaken the whole community.

He said: “You can feel it in the air that every parent saw their child in this event.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Janessa’s family has launched a fundraiser to help cover the unexpected costs following her death. It has raised around $3,000 so far.



The family said: “No family is ever prepared to say goodbye to a child, especially so suddenly and so young.”

News.title: Three-year BAN on fireworks and BBQs in parks is approved across major UK city – and ignoring risks a £1,000 fine
News.content:
A MAJOR UK city has imposed a three-year ban on the use of disposable barbecues in parks over the risk of wildfires.

Under the new rules, those caught lighting the portable grills in most of the city’s open spaces could face fines.

Oxford City Council has approved a three-year ban on disposable barbecues, open fires and fireworks under a new Public Space Protection Order (PSPO).



Applying to 41 sites across the city, including many of Oxford’s parks and open spaces, those caught lighting open fires, barbecues, lanterns or fireworks may risk fines of £100.



The new rules are set to be implemented from tomorrow (September 4), in a bid to help “reduce the risk of wildfires”, according to the council.

This comes as the Met Office declared five heatwaves this summer, with the dry weather sparking wildfires across the country.

A report by council officers added that the sites were selected as a result of footfall and “risk of ignition”.



The report also noted that “in the absence of a PSPO, the risk of fires started by barbecues, open fires, lanterns and fireworks would increase”.

Failure to pay the penalty, or if found to have caused serious damage, may also lead to prosecution and fines of up to £1,000.

Councillor Anna Railton, cabinet member for planning and zero carbon Oxford said: “Oxford is fortunate to have so many beautiful green spaces at the heart of the city, but that also increases the risk of fires spreading to nearby homes and properties.

“We have therefore reluctantly taken the decision to increase the powers available to tackle reckless behaviour.



“Enforcement action is always a last resort, but these powers are there if needed to protect people’s homes, our green spaces and wildlife habitats that are already under significant pressure.”

Despite the new rules, the city council has confirmed that long-running fireworks events, such as the Oxford Roundtable fireworks show, will take place.

This is as a result of the “reasonable justification” clause in the order which allows for planned and sanctioned activities to go ahead.

News.title: Lamborghinis & Mercedes G-Wagons seized by cops after dropping to 17mph, wheel-spinning & weaving across major motorway
News.content:
LUXURY motors have been seized by cops after they were caught wheel-spinning, weaving and slowing down to speeds of 17mph on a major motorway.

One clip shows Lamborghinis and a Mercedes G-Wagon being stopped by police in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, on Wednesday evening.



Cops shared the footage, which was captured just before 7pm, on social media after a number of people were prosecuted for driving dangerously on the M66 and M62.

The high-powered supercars were first spotted speeding on the M66 motorway last night.



Police said the cars were seen weaving across lanes, wheel spinning and slowing down to speeds of around 17mph on the motorway.

The vehicles were then spotted on the M62, with officers deployed to bring them to a stop.

Two Lamborghinis were stopped as they came off the motorway.

Officers then brought the remaining vehicles to a stop on Edinburgh Way in Rochdale.



Five Lamborghini’s and a Mercedes G-Wagon were seized and police prosecuted the drivers for a number of driving offences.

Alongside the clip, a GMP spokesperson wrote: “Last night (Wednesday 2 September 2026) some Lamborghini drivers thought they were on an episode of Drive to Survive. Spoiler alert: they weren’t.”

They added: “The only pitstop they are making is to the vehicle impound.”

Chief Inspector Danny Kabal, from GMP’s Transport Policing and Crime command said: “We take road safety very serious in GMP, and we will not tolerate careless, inconsiderate, anti-social or dangerous driving on our roads.

“Recent changes to Section 59 of the Police Reform Act now enables us to seize vehicles without having to issue a warning first.



He added: “People who think it is acceptable to use our roads as a racetrack, need to pay attention to this result and take it as a warning – they will have their vehicles seized and they will be prosecuted. Where proportionate to do so, they will also be arrested.

“I would like to thank the members of the public who reported this matter to us and apologise to them for any inconvenience caused when we temporarily shut the road to deal with the offenders.

“If anyone has any footage of this incident, including dashcam or CCTV, please get in touch with us via 101 or our website: gmp.police.uk. I would also urge anyone who witnesses such poor driving or riding on our roads to report it to us.”

Last month, a convoy of supercars were seized by cops as they were heading to a wedding after they were spotted being driven dangerously on two motorways.

The “rolling supercar showcase” put other road users in danger as it drove to the pal’s big day along the M4 and M5, police said.



The impounded high-performance vehicles include a £240,000 Lamborghini Huracán LP 640-4 Performante Spyder and a £110,000 Audi R8 Spyder.

And in July, 13 supercars worth more than £2.5million were seized by police after another convoy was spotted driving dangerously on a major UK motorway.

The high-octane motors impounded on that occasion included seven Lamborghinis, four Audi R8s, a Ferrari , and a Porsche .

Police gave each driver a warning for anti-social driving after being alerted by motorists to a string of dangerous manoeuvres.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The supercars accelerated to excessive speeds before suddenly braking, bunching together and disrupting traffic, witnesses said.



Drivers even allegedly used the hard shoulder to undertake other motorists.

News.title: Putin's nuclear bomber commander 'shot in head and abdomen' during 'ambush'
News.content:
Putin's nuclear bomber commander 'shot in head and abdomen' during 'ambush'

A shooter is said to have ambushed Putin's nuclear bomber commander Nikolai Varpakhovich near a private residence in the Saratov Oblast in Russia's southwest

View 2 Images Putin's nuclear bomber commander was reportedly shot twice outside a private residence in the Engels district (Image: Mikhail Metzel/Pool Sputnik Krem)

A Russian general in charge of Putin's nuclear bombers has reportedly been shot in the head and stomach in the Saratov Oblast, southwestern Russia.

‌



Major General Nikolai Varpakhovich is said to be in a critical condition after an unidentified motorcyclist opened fire outside a private residence in the Engels district.

‌



Two shots were reportedly fired from a pistol, with the general struck in the head and abdomen - and no suspect apprehended at this stage.

‌



The Russian Investigative Committee said a probe had been launched into the attempted murder of a military service member who was shot several times in the city of Engels in the Saratov region on Thursday.

While the committee did not name the military service member, Russian telegram channels widely reported it was Mr Varpakhovich.

View 2 Images Putin has raced growing criticism over his war on Ukraine (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The incident comes as Russia faces growing criticism over its war on Ukraine, including from within the country itself.

Anti-war politician Lev Shlosberg, the 63-year-old deputy leader of a Russian party, Yabloko, was convicted of spreading false information about the conflict after speaking out against Russian strikes on Ukraine.

Shlosberg said before sentencing: "The very concept of a crime, understood as an act that poses a genuine danger to society, has been distorted in this country.

‌



"Under these new laws, crimes now include the free expression of peaceful convictions, standing up for human dignity, protesting against violence, refusing to accept lies, and showing compassion, empathy and mercy towards others.

"Virtue is persecuted, while vice is encouraged and exalted."

Putin has tightened restrictions on dissent since the invasion began, with authorities repeatedly targeting those who publicly challenge the Kremlin's narrative.

‌



Yet on Thursday, Putin acknowledged that Moscow had underestimated Ukraine's ability to strike energy facilities on Russian territory.

Kyiv has increasingly focused its attacks on Russia's oil and energy infrastructure, saying the strikes are intended to disrupt the recourses that help fund Moscow's war effort.

The attacks have come alongside repeated large-scale Russian bombardments of Ukrainian cities and crucial infrastructure.

Article continues below

The escalation has also raised concerns over the safety of civilian aviation.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned this week that Russian airspace could no longer be considered safe and called on airlines to avoid routes over the country as the conflict continues to spill beyond the battlefield.

He said: "We want to warn every airline that uses Russian airspace, every insurer, everyone who still uses key Russian airports: the Russian sky is becoming completely dangerous."

News.title: Meghan Markle pays tribute to her ‘friend and mentor’ Gloria Steinem with emotional post
News.content:
Meghan Markle pays tribute to her ‘friend and mentor’ Gloria Steinem with emotional post

The Duchess of Sussex has shared a moving post to feminist campaigner and author Gloria Steinem, who has died at the age of 92, as she recalled her ‘very favourite story’ about the activist

View 6 Images Meghan and Gloria met in 2020 and forged a strong friendship (Image: meghan/Instagram)

Meghan Markle has paid tribute to her ‘friend and mentor’ Gloria Steinem, who has passed away at the age of 92. The feminist campaigner and author “passed away peacefully at her home in New York City, surrounded by some of the many who loved her", according to a statement.

‌



Steinem was remembered as one of the trailblazers for women's equality after she died on Wednesday in New York City. She dedicated her life to advocating and campaigning for a number of issues including equal pay and reproductive rights.

‌



The Duchess of Sussex had a long friendship with Steinem, as she recalled her ‘very favourite story’ about the activist and author in a lengthy social media post. Meghan posted three photos to her Instagram, one of which shows a picture of a photo frame containing a snap of Steinem with Prince Archie when he was little.

‌



King Charles to welcome Sultan of Oman for State Visit as he returns to work after Balmoral break READ MORE :

View 6 Images Meghan has paid tribute to her friend Gloria Steinem, who has passed away at the age of 92 (Image: meghan/Instagram)

The other two photos show the two women together, one where they are smiling and posing for the camera, while the other shows the two women sitting outside deep in candid conversation. To accompany the post, Meghan added the song Just Because I'm a Woman by Dolly Parton.

In her lengthy and emotional caption, the duchess recalled some of Steinem’s pioneering work, and recalled some of the sweet moments they shared together. Meghan wrote: “Celebrating the life and legacy of my friend and mentor, Gloria Steinem, and also grateful to know that in these last few weeks and days she knew exactly how loved and admired she was.

‌



“You all know her many accolades and the way in which she helped shape the world for women and all people - ‘we are linked, not ranked’ she would tell me, and the bracelet she gave me said exactly that. I still wear it with pride.

The Duchess continued: “Publicly, we did interviews together, called young voters to encourage them to have their voices heard, attended award ceremonies, and brainstormed how to help this beautiful yet complicated world to become more equitable.

6 View 6 Images The Duchess shared a photo of Gloria with Archie when he was a toddler (Image: meghan/Instagram) 6 View 6 Images Gloria presented Meghan with an award in 2023 (Image: Getty Images Ms. Foundation for Women)

‌



“But privately, she was even better than you would imagine- spending Thanksgiving with our family, introducing me to one of my best friends (forever the champion of female friendship), loving our children with her whole heart, counselling me during hard times, and giving extraordinary advice and perspective with a cup of tea and an unrivalled cheekiness and wit.”

Meghan then spoke about her ‘very favourite story’ about her friend, as she recalled: “When she was out one day in NY, and a woman approached her in absolute awe and said she wanted to introduce her young daughter to her (though she was embarrassed to say the young girl may not know who she was).

“Gloria replied: ‘It doesn’t matter if she knows who I am. What matters is that she knows who SHE is.’ Rest in peace, and rest in pride. Look at what you’ve done for all of us. Thank you,” Meghan concluded the post.

‌



View 6 Images Meghan praised her pioneering work in women's rights (Image: meghan/Instagram)

Meghan has previously spoken fondly of Steinem, as she said in an interview with Vogue in 2022: "She reminds me that when you have anger, you have to channel that energy into something that makes a difference. That’s what activism is. It’s about how we show up."

Steinem and Meghan met shortly after the Duke and Duchess moved to California in 2020 after quitting their royal roles, and quickly formed a strong friendship. Steinem, who co-founded the Ms. Foundation, presented Meghan with a 2023 Women of Vision award, for her global advocacy to empower and advocate on behalf of women and girls.

‌



During her acceptance speech, Meghan said, "Thank you for the leadership that has brought all of us here tonight. And to my friend Gloria for the inspiration that you are, for your mentorship, your sage advice, your extraordinarily cheeky sense of humour, and of course, for your incredible friendship: Thank you."

View 6 Images Meghan praised Gloria on stage for her 'inspiration' and 'sage advice' (Image: Getty Images Ms. Foundation for Women)

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Steinem rose to prominence in the late 1960s and early 1970s, during the second wave of feminism. One of her most ground-breaking pieces was produced back in 1963, when she went undercover as a Playboy bunny for 11 days and penned a two-part exposé of the eye-opening experience.

News of Steinem’s death was announced this morning in a statement shared on her Instagram account which said: “Gloria’s near-century on earth were years well-lived, and she continued working for equality until the very end. Gloria’s greatest gift was her ability to listen to others, to make others feel seen and heard.

"Her words, actions and example gave people permission to be their truest selves. Gloria lived true to her independent spirit, always with curiosity and a great sense of humour.” Tributes have poured in for the pioneering activist from actors Sandra Bullock and Julianne Moore, singer-songwriter Patti Smith and former US secretary of state Hillary Clinton.

News.title: Households urged to do 'simplest' step to avoid bins not being collected or fines
News.content:
Households urged to do 'simplest' step to avoid bins not being collected or fines

Putting the wrong items in the wrong bins means they are likely not to be collected - and could even result in a fine

View 2 Images There are many bin rules to follow (Image: richard johnson via Getty Images)

For millions of households across the UK, bin day can feel like a weekly challenge. With separate containers now required for general rubbish, food waste, recycling, garden cuttings and more, it is little wonder so many people get it wrong.

‌



And the consequences of making a mistake can be surprisingly serious. A bin placed out with the wrong contents may simply be left on the kerb uncollected, leaving you with a growing pile of rubbish until the lorry comes round again.

‌



In serious cases, your local council could even hit you with an £80 fine. England has seen significant changes to its waste system this year, with councils introducing new separate collections for food waste, paper and card, glass, and metal and plastic packaging as part of a national drive to improve recycling.

‌



So what is the best way to stay on top of it all? According to one waste collector, the answer could not be more straightforward.

View 2 Images It is important not to get it wrong (Image: petekarici via Getty Images)

Ashley, better known as the No. 1 Binman on TikTok, says there is one simple move every household should make — check their council's website.

‌



"You just need to go to your council website, it is that simple," he said. "Most councils have an A-Z on what goes in what bin or if it can go in any bin. It has all the information on there."

Ashley is also keen to stress that bin rules are not universal — what applies in one area may be completely different just a few miles away.

"Every council is different," he explained. "Just because if at one house you used to put something in the bin, it doesn't mean anything. As soon as you move councils, [it is] completely different."

‌



The council website will also flag what to do if your bin was not collected, and when your next scheduled collection day falls.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

What happens if you put the wrong items in your bin?

Beyond the inconvenience of a missed collection, there are more serious repercussions for households that repeatedly fall foul of waste rules. Contaminated recycling — where the wrong materials are mixed in — can spoil entire lorry loads, leading councils to refuse collection altogether.

Article continues below

When this happens, your bin may be tagged with a warning notice and you will be asked to remove the offending items before the next collection date.

The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (DEFRA) confirms that councils are legally entitled to issue fixed penalty notices where households repeatedly ignore waste collection regulations, or where rubbish causes an obstruction or nuisance to others.

However, a fine will not be issued without warning. Councils must first provide a written notice explaining the breach. If the issue continues, a notice of intent is issued, followed by a final notice 28 days later confirming the penalty amount. The maximum fine that can be handed out is £80.

News.title: Parents cook three separate meals at dinnertime as fussy eaters add stress
News.content:
Parents cook three separate meals at dinnertime as fussy eaters add stress

More than half of parents find family mealtimes stressful as four in 10 households are cooking multiple meals to keep everyone happy.

View 3 Images Four in 10 families prepare at least three different meals at dinnertime (Image: Getty Images)

Four in 10 families prepare at least three different meals at dinnertime, as mums and dads navigate varying tastes, schedules and dietary requirements under one roof. The typical household cook spends an additional 30 minutes in the kitchen each week attempting to satisfy everyone's demands, with 60% feeling under pressure to make mealtimes work for the entire family.

‌



The study of 2,000 parents with children aged 0 to 18 revealed that, overall, more than half (53%) find mealtimes stressful. Despite this, 93% believe it's vital their family spends time together at dinner - even if not everyone is eating the same thing.

‌



The study was commissioned by Dolmio, which has joined forces with podcaster and mum Giovanna Fletcher to mark its 40th anniversary and the comeback of Mama and Papa to our screens after more than a decade away.

‌



Giovanna said: "Mama and Papa Dolmio, and the whole Dolmio family, have been such iconic characters since I was a child, so I loved being part of their return."

View 3 Images Mama & Papa Dolmio were sotted in London with Giovanna Fletcher (Image: PinPep)

"As a mum myself, I know how precious dinnertime can be," Fletcher added, "it's often one of the few moments in the day when everyone can come together, catch up and connect.

‌



"As Dolmio celebrates its 40th anniversary, it feels like the perfect opportunity to celebrate those simple family moments that make dinnertime so special."

Three quarters of those surveyed agreed that dinnertime at home has become more flexible and less rigid than it was during their childhood.

Over a third of Baby Boomers (34%) believe family mealtimes have transformed significantly since they raised young children, with nearly half (48%) stating families dine together less frequently than before.

‌



Meanwhile, Millennials highlighted how families now enjoy a broader range of cuisines and dishes compared with their own upbringing (39%).

View 3 Images Dolmio is celebrating its 40th anniversary (Image: PinPep)

The research also revealed the typical family shares the same meal together just four times weekly, with a quarter regularly having to accommodate fussy or particular eaters.

‌



Hectic household schedules (33%), children having greater influence over their food choices (30%) and parents having reduced time to cook from scratch (28%) were amongst the primary factors driving this transformation.

A quarter of families regularly depend on pre-made sauces (25%), ready meals (19%) and meal kits (16%) to help put dinner on the table.

Overall, 51% believe households are less inclined to eat dinner simultaneously now compared with four decades ago.

‌



While over a fifth (22%) want mealtimes to focus more on spending quality time together over the next 40 years, rather than what everyone is consuming.

Hana Hutchinson, a spokesperson for Dolmio, said: "While modern mealtimes can sometimes be chaotic, they are still seen as integral - even when I look at my own family, the juggle of daily life and growing children means tastes and favourites change in an instant.

"But what has remained is the dinner table, the place where, no matter the after-school sport club, friend visit or parent returning from work, it is the one moment to connect.

Article continues below

"That's why, for 40 years, Dolmio has championed that there is no right way or rulebook to follow when it comes to preparing dinner – instead, it is about doing it your way, whatever is right for your family."

News.title: Three-day-old baby ‘died in doctor’s arms’ after mum ‘repeatedly ignored’ by medics
News.content:
Three-day-old baby ‘died in doctor’s arms’ after mum ‘repeatedly ignored’ by medics

Julie Keegan, 35, described a “horror scene” as medical staff acted “like headless chickens” while three-day-old Mason McLean lay dying after she repeatedly raised concerns about his health.

View 4 Images Mum Julie and baby Mason (Image: Glasgow Live)

A mum has described the horrific moment her baby died in the arms of a doctor after her repeated concerns about his health were allegedly dismissed by medical staff.

‌



Julie Keegan, 35, said her baby boy Mason McLean would still be alive if “one person had done their job” and taken her warnings seriously.

‌



Mason was just three days old when he tragically passed away in January 2023, after mum Julie and dad Angus McLean, 31, rushed him to A&E after he grew cold and stopped feeding.

‌



The mum described staff at Glasgow’s Queen Elizabeth University Hospital acting like "headless chickens" when Mason stopped breathing. She said Mason's last moments were a "horror scene" as chaotic staff allegedly argued over how to correctly perform CPR on an infant.

View 4 Images Baby Mason died in 2023 (Image: Glasgow Live)

NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde has apologised for the missed opportunities in Mason's care, and says it has since taken measures to improve its training and processes, Glasgow Live reports.

‌



Mason was "completely healthy" when he was born on January 29, 2023 at the nearby Princess Royal Maternity Hospital, but Julie noticed something was wrong the night he came home from the hospital.

Julie, who is an ICU nurse, said: "He was doing brilliant, and then the first night he was home, I noticed he became unwell straight away. He was like a different baby. He was a lot colder and unable to feed."

Julie said a routine visit from the midwife the following day was the beginning of his fatal illness being dismissed as "normal newborn behaviour."

‌



She says the midwife mistook Mason's sepsis symptoms for jaundice, and decided not to refer him to the hospital. The midwife said she would pay the family another visit the following day, but Mason didn't make it through the night. Julie said: "[The midwife] left me with a baby that was dying of sepsis, and said 'I'll just be back tomorrow'."

View 4 Images Dad Angus and Mason (Image: Glasgow Live)

After several unsuccessful phone calls to medics Angus and Julie were eventually advised to go to A&E at the Queen Elizabeth University Hospital by NHS 24. By this point, Mason was "clammy, having difficulty breathing" and had stopped wetting his nappies.

‌



Julie, who has since had two more children with partner Angus, said: "It was only because I was getting upset that they allowed us to go to the hospital for Mason to get checked over.

"I think they should've sent an ambulance, if someone says their baby is finding it difficult to breathe. And he died within six hours [of that call].

After a "horrible", frantic drive in rush-hour traffic to the Queen Elizabeth, they arrived at A&E where Mason was seen to straight away - though the care he received was "very, very poor", Julie said.

‌



Julie also said Mason's face had begun seizing and she was told by hospital staff that "all babies make funny faces", and that she was praised for having such a quiet, "well behaved" baby - when in fact "he was dying and he couldn't react because he was so sick".

View 4 Images Mason died partly due to sepsis (Image: Glasgow Live)

Julie says Mason was then taken to the special care baby unit, and claims the nurse didn't take his observations. A reflex test showed that Mason was extremely weak at this point, and the doctor advised that he "just needed a really good feed". The doctor then left the ward, Julie said.

‌



She eventually came back to take Mason's observations, when Julie said he let out a "gasp", which she believes was his last breath. "I remember thinking, 'there's no way a doctor can have a baby in her arms and for him not to be breathing'. I had a lot more faith in them than I should've."

Julie explains what happened next as a "horror scene." She said the doctor began "screaming" Mason's name, running up and down the room and to the resuscitation room shouting "how do you turn this equipment on?".

The nurse and doctor began arguing about how to do CPR on a baby, Julie claims. She added: "It was like a horror scene, they weren't doing any compressions. It was so bad. They were like headless chickens. The doctor was a deer in the headlights.

‌



"My baby was dying in front of my eyes."

Julie says the correct resuscitation equipment was not on the ward, and staff had to go to two different floors to get it, which the mum described as "appalling".

"That could've been the difference between his heart getting started straight away and his heart getting started five minutes later. And then the doctor said there was nothing more they could do and that we had to say goodbye."

‌



Since the loss of their first child, Mason's parents have been pushing for change in maternity services, and met with Health Secretary Angela Constance this week. Julie said: "I told every single person that he was sick and everything that was wrong with him, and I was made out to be insane, and as an overprotective first-time mum.

"If anybody had done their job that night, he would still be alive… It shouldn't be a lottery if your child lives or dies depending who's on shift that night."

Julie and Angus have also launched the Mason Matters campaign to advocate for reform to maternity care in Scotland.

‌



A spokesperson for NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde said: "We continue to extend our heartfelt condolences to Mason McLean's family. While we are unable to comment on individual cases due to patient confidentiality, we again sincerely apologise for the missed opportunities in Mason's care.

"A Significant Adverse Event Review (SAER) was completed in August 2025 and improvements to processes, training and equipment, have been implemented.

"We also strengthened our neonatal guidance, updated clinical pathways, and enhanced processes for temperature monitoring and clinical observations to help improve the care provided to newborn babies.

Article continues below

"A SAER is a formal review process that examines significant adverse events to understand what happened, identify learning, and support improvements that help prevent similar incidents from happening again."

News.title: Dad murdered sex worker then daughter helped him dump body in canal using paving slabs
News.content:
Dad murdered sex worker then daughter helped him dump body in canal using paving slabs

John Anslow and his daughter, Hayley-Marie Ferguson, have been convicted after mum Chereiss Bailey, 36, was killed and dumped in a canal in West Bromwich

View 3 Images Chereiss Bailey, 36, had 'a huge personality' and a 'beautiful heart', her family said (Image: West Midlands Police)

A man has been found guilty of murdering a "much-loved" woman before dumping her body in a canal with the help of his daughter.

Chereiss Bailey, 36, from Tipton, was last seen alive on the afternoon of September 27 last year, with her body later found on October 7. John Anslow, 65. "subjected her to a traumatic assault" at his home on Stour Street in West Bromwich on September 27, police said.

The following morning, Anslow, who was disabled, cancelled his community carers and called his daughter, 42-year-old Hayley-Marie Ferguson, for help. She took a taxi to his home and brought paving slabs with her.

After helping to clean the property and remove incriminating evidence, Ferguson attended a Peaky Blinders event that evening in fancy dress, Birmingham Live reports.

She later returned to her father's home and the pair placed Ms Bailey's body in Anslow's wheelchair before pushing it to a spot on the Walsall Canal known as 'Eight Locks', near Ryders Green Road. They used a washing line with paving slabs attached to submerge the body in the water.

View 3 Images John Anslow, 65, has been found guilty of murder (Image: West Midlands Police)

During a trial at Birmingham Crown Court, prosecutor Michael Duck KC told a jury that Ms Bailey, a vulnerable person who lived alone, had occasionally worked as a sex worker.

Anslow had denied murder but was found guilty on Tuesday following a three-week trial. He had already admitted preventing the lawful and decent burial of a body.

Ferguson, 42, of Heronville Road, West Bromwich, was found guilty of preventing the lawful and decent burial of a body and assisting an offender. She was not accused of taking part in Ms Bailey’s murder.

The pair are due to be sentenced at a later date.

West Midlands Police said a member of the public reported on October 4 last year that a woman had been killed and her body had been "disposed of" in the canal network in Great Bridge.

Ms Bailey's body was found submerged in the canal on October 7, with a washing line cord attached to paving slabs.

In a statement, Ms Bailey's family said: "Chereiss was a much-loved daughter, sister, mother, auntie, granddaughter and friend, but those words alone could never explain what she meant to us.

"She had a huge personality, a beautiful heart and a way of making her presence known wherever she went. Life was never quiet when Chereiss was around, and we would give absolutely anything to have that noise back."

View 3 Images Hayley-Marie Ferguson and her dad 'hatched a sickening plot to dispose of Chereiss' body', police said (Image: West Midlands Police)

They continued: "The hardest part is knowing how much life she still had left to live. There should have been more birthdays, more Christmases, more laughter, more family memories and so many ordinary days that we never imagined we would have to live without her.

"Most heartbreaking of all, her little boy has been robbed of growing up with his mum beside him. We will make sure he grows up knowing exactly who she was, how much she adored him and how fiercely she was loved.

"We want Chereiss remembered for Chereiss. For her smile, her humour, her kindness, her love for her family and all the little things that made her who she was."

Det Insp Michelle Cordell said: "It is difficult to comprehend the abhorrent actions of John Anslow and his daughter Hayley Ferguson late September last year.

“Anslow had presented himself as a vulnerable wheelchair user with extremely limited mobility. He was in fact a violent predator. His daughter Hayley had also presented as having limited mobility, evidence of which proves otherwise.

“Chereiss was killed in John Anslow’s home and we may never know what motivated him to commit such an awful attack on a woman."

Article continues below

She added: "Our team have worked relentlessly to gather and present evidence shown during this trial. I hope today’s verdict provides some comfort to Chereiss’ family who have acted with incredible dignity and restraint throughout this difficult process, and who continue to grieve her loss."

News.title: 'Bubbly' mum killed in Middlesbrough house fire with niece had only recently married
News.content:
'Bubbly' mum killed in Middlesbrough house fire with niece had only recently married

Natalie McDonald, 34, died alongside her seven-year-old niece Valentina Foster in the Grangetown house fire near Middlesbrough.

View Image Natalie McDonald died in a house fire in Middlesbrough along with her seven-year-old niece (Image: Cleveland Police)

A heartbroken family today told how the victim of a house fire on Teesside 'sparkled like a shining beauty' at her wedding just nine months ago.

Natalie McDonald, 34, tragically died alongside seven-year-old Valentina Foster in Birchington Avenue, Grangetown last Wednesday.

Jaden Wright, of no fixed abode, appeared in court earlier today, charged with both murders.

Natalie’s family said: "Natalie Louise was known by everyone as Natalie Louise Kirton, she is Natalie Louise McDonald having married Anthony McDonald only nine months ago.

"She had the biggest, most beautiful wedding; she sparkled like the shining beauty she was. She was loved by everyone, she was bright, bubbly and full of life, the heart and soul of our street and community, loved by all.

"Her family has lost its beautiful, kind soul. She was the life and soul of every party, and she will be sadly missed by our family, her two brothers and sister, all who are broken.

"Her nieces and nephews, with her being such a big part of their lives, being like a second mother to them. Her nana, grandad, mam and dad are all heartbroken. Our Nat will be forever missed."

They said Natalie's daughter, who cannot be named due to a court order, will "forever miss" her mother.

Article continues below

Wright, 23, also stands accused of two counts of Section 18 GBH with intent and two counts of attempted Section 18 GBH with intent.

A man and a woman remain in hospital receiving treatment for injuries sustained in the house fire, Cleveland Police said today.

News.title: Major Royal Mail update for anyone sending parcels or letters
News.content:
Major Royal Mail update for anyone sending parcels or letters

Royal Mail confirmed the new service on Thursday

View Image Here's what Royal Mail has said (Image: Alena Kravchenko via Getty Images)

Royal Mail has issued a major update to anyone sending letters or parcels, or returning items.

‌



The company has unveiled a new location finder designed to "make it easier than ever for customers" to track down their nearest drop-off, collection or returns point for parcels. The Find Royal Mail Locations tool, available on the postal service's website, comes following a significant expansion of the company's network, which now includes lockers, Royal Mail Shops and parcel postboxes. Customers can search by postcode or via an interactive map, using advanced filters to pinpoint their most convenient option based on service type, including collection, parcel drop-off or purchasing postage; parcel size; and opening hours.

‌



Royal Mail boasts the UK's largest out-of-home network, with around 30,000 parcel points, including lockers, shops and parcel postboxes. The company remains on track to reach 45,000 out-of-home locations by 2030, it confirmed in an update on Thursday.

‌



The Find Royal Mail Locations tool has been rolled out as part of Royal Mail's commitment to making sending and returning parcels as straightforward as possible for customers.

Mike Richmond, chief customer officer at Royal Mail, said: "People are shopping online and using second-hand marketplaces more and more, meaning they need convenient options to send and collect their parcels. We've massively expanded our network to give customers more choice.

Article continues below

"Find Royal Mail Locations makes it easier than ever to find the best option, whatever the size of parcel or time of day."

News.title: Andy Burnham praises UK-EU ties in meeting with Emmanuel Macron
News.content:
"It shows what collaboration can achieve, just as we are also showing on Ukraine, on small boats, and also on strengthening the UK-EU relationship," Burnham added.

Macron said: "This is a very strong relationship. For me it is extremely important, and I'm here with willingness and a commitment to get closer."

The French leader's visit to the UK was primarily to mark the Bayeux Tapestry's loan to the British Museum. He met King Charles at the museum on Wednesday, ahead of the medieval tapestry going on public display next week.

In bilateral talks on Thursday, Burnham and Macron discussed not only small boats but also the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, as well as defence and EU co-operation.

The arrival of the first foreign leader under the Burnham premiership is an important symbolic moment - it shows the relationship with Paris is an important priority.

But it also reflects an obvious reality - to further reduce small boats crossings, working with France will be essential.

France and the UK have been working extremely closely on Ukraine and Iran, trying to jointly influence the White House.

And Paris will be an important player as the UK seeks even stronger economic ties with Europe under the new No 10 administration.

The "mega dinghies" crossing the Channel illegally - first seen earlier in August with a 15-metre long vessel carrying a record 230 migrants towards the UK - are arguably the most pressing challenge facing the pair.

It follows a summer when the overall number of small boat arrivals in the UK fell to a seven-year low.

News.title: Badenoch accuses Burnham of kicking defence spending into the long grass
News.content:
Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch has accused the prime minister of "kicking defence spending into the long grass" as she set out Tory plans to push the figure to 3% of GDP by 2030.

Badenoch said a Conservative government would fund the commitment, worth Â£10bn a year, through measures including reimposing the two-child benefit cap, reforming housing benefit and ending VAT exemptions for Motability cars.

Pointing to the threat from countries like Russia and Iran, Badenoch told a press conference: "Conflict is coming, we must act now."

So far Andy Burnham's government has only committed to setting out a plan in the spring to meet the Nato target of spending 3.5% of GDP on defence by 2035.

Speaking at an event in central London, Badenoch said: "Andy Burnham is kicking defence spending into the long grass.

"Our enemies are not going to sit around and wait for Labour to find the money to fight them."

Burnham has pointed to his choice of Chancellor, John Healey, who quit as defence secretary in June over the last government's failure to commit to a 3% increase, as proof of his commitment to defence investment.

However, Badenoch said the prime minister should call a general election if he is not willing to find the money now, adding that Healey's decision to quit over defence spending appeared to have changed since he became chancellor.

"He resigned because Britain was not on track to reach 3% by 2030 and I praised him at the time for that decision," she said.

"Now that he is chancellor he does not seem to believe that any more and I am concerned he has been bought off with a promotion."

News.title: Schools to close early for A66 crash funeral amid safety concerns
News.content:
Supt John Wrintmore from Cleveland Police said there was potential for traffic disruption and delays from 15:00 to 17:00 on Friday.

"This will affect areas of South Bank, Normanby Road through Teesville, Ormesby and Marton, and Acklam Road," he said.

"We are working closely with highways departments from the local authority, who are leading on the traffic management for this event, in order to minimise disruption.

"As with any significant gathering, we have plans in place to ensure public safety and security, which is line with our usual process."

A spokesperson for Redcar & Cleveland Borough Council said: "A number of schools in the South Bank area will close earlier than usual on Friday afternoon due to anticipated traffic congestion and transport disruption associated with a local funeral taking place in the area.

"The decision was made after careful consideration of the potential impact on home-to-school transport and the departure of pupils, staff and families at the end of the school day.

"Schools have worked with the Local Authority and transport providers to consider arrangements for pupils, including those who travel to and from specialist educational settings.

"We recognise that early closure may cause inconvenience for some parents and carers, and we thank them for their understanding and cooperation."

The decision comes after a vigil, for one of the young men who died, last week was followed by disorder in Haswell, County Durham, where a number of cars were set on fire.

The incident prompted criticism from MPs and police.

The Volkswagen Passat involved in the collision was being pursued by police until 10 seconds before the crash, according to the police watchdog.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct said the Passat was believed to be using cloned registration plates.

A total of 27 people have been arrested as part of a wider police operation against organised crime, following the crash.
