Liverpool’s outlay did not include a right back, defensive midfielder or right-winger but Iraola, who believes Barcola could be deployed in Mohamed Salah’s old position, insists the club’s approach was correct.

“I’m very happy with all the signings we’ve made,” said the Liverpool head coach. “I know the next question: ‘Do you want more signings in other positions?’ At the end the club has decided those signings we have done are the ones that improved our team and our position.

“There were other options we decided not to take, for different reasons: sometimes it is sporting reasons because they don’t improve what you have, sometimes it is economical reasons as it didn’t make sense in terms of the market to do those movements. But I’m happy now I know what we have, I have a lot of quality in the team and now it is the moment for us, for the players, for me to develop what we have.”

Despite the absence of a natural right-winger – Liverpool explored deals for Yankuba Minteh at Brighton and Ismaïla Sarr at Crystal Palace – Iraola is confident Barcola, Victor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha can provide sufficient cover.

He said: “I think we’ve preferred at the end to have the best players, probably, than a player that maybe is specifically for that [right-sided] position. I’m very used from my previous teams to demand for all the wingers to play both sides.

“Probably all of them have played more on the left, but I would say I’ve seen them in a good place on the right. Probably Rio is more specific from the left side, but I think he has also showed the willingness to improve and play on the right. Even Bradley, he’s very open and I think he can play right and left. He started actually more on the right side when he started with Olympique Lyonnais. I’m happy with the four wingers we have and I’m sure we are going to be able to cover those two positions.”

Sports.title: Arsenal bank on continuity after big names elude them late in transfer window
Sports.content:
When Mikel Arteta revealed before Arsenal’s win at Aston Villa that he had pleaded with the Premier League to introduce bigger matchday squads, the final 24 hours of the transfer window was not quite what he would have had in mind. A deadline day on which Manchester City matched the British record to sign Enzo Fernández from Chelsea for £125m came and went as Arsenal allowed Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri to leave without bringing in replacements.

With Gabriel Martinelli expected to join Al-Hilal before Sunday’s deadline in Saudi Arabia for a fee that could rise to £60m, there are question marks about the depth of the champions’ squad, despite Arteta still having at least two options for each position. Eberechi Eze will provide competition on the left for the new boy Christos Tzolis, and the manager has a plethora of central midfielders at his disposal after the arrival of Bruno Guimarães from Newcastle, but there is not much room for manoeuvre should Arsenal experience injuries in attack like they have for the past two seasons.

Arteta had been clear after the Villa game when asked whether he hoped to bring in more players. “We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions in the manner that we play as well, so we’re going to try to do that,” he said.

Yet none arrived as Arsenal passed up the opportunity to bring in Malick Fofana owing to what it is understood were Arteta’s doubts over whether the Belgium forward would improve the squad, with Sunderland eventually beating Crystal Palace to his signature in dramatic scenes. The fallout has prompted some Arsenal supporters to question the wisdom of spending most of the summer, after missing out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea, chasing “dream” transfer targets such as Vinícius Júnior and Julián Alvarez, with the sporting director, Andrea Berta, most in the firing line.

The Italian’s arrival from Atlético Madrid in March 2025 was heralded as a coup by many. Berta’s decisiveness last summer enabled Arsenal to rack up a net spend of more than £250m – comfortably outstripping their rivals – on players such as Eze, Viktor Gyökeres and Martín Zubimendi.

This summer the Premier League champions were quick off the mark to replace Leandro Trossard with Tzolis, then added Guimarães, before buying Ezri Konsa to cover the long-term absence of William Saliba, but the lack of attacking reinforcements on deadline day was eye-catching.

Offloading Jesus, one of the club’s highest earners, saved wages, and Martinelli’s departure as the club’s record sale would reduce Arsenal’s net spend to £78m – less than Brentford’s – compared with £162m at City, who spent more than £300m recalibrating their midfield. Iliman Ndiaye, who joined City from Everton for £65m, was another player on Arsenal’s shortlist who they opted against.

View image in fullscreen Gabriel Martinelli is poised to leave Arsenal without a direct replacement being in place. Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty Images

There can be no questioning Kroenke Sports Entertainment’s commitment to the cause, Arsenal having the second-highest net spend over past five seasons at more than £680m. Yet it will not have escaped the attention of some fans that it was confirmed on deadline day that KSE will expand its sporting empire with the purchase of the Major League Baseball side the Los Angeles Angels, for a reported $4bn (£3bn). With an estimated value of $26bn, it is not as if it cannot afford that.

Even before Arsenal wrapped up their first title for 22 years in May, the co-chair Josh Kroenke promised that “there will be no standing still when the season ends”, and bringing in Premier League-ready players such as Konsa and Guimarães was a statement of intent. However, the inability to attract real star quality in attack is an issue considering the heavy burden on Bukayo Saka after a couple of injury-hit campaigns. Kenan Yildiz could have fitted the bill but Juventus were not interested in selling the Turkey forward, and Alvarez made plain he wanted only Barcelona.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Arsenal struggled to break teams down during the second half of last season and became heavily reliant on their set-piece prowess, although a rejuvenated Martin Ødegaard has started the campaign promisingly.

Martinelli has failed in recent seasons to replicate his form of the 2022-23 season, when he scored 15 Premier League goals, but his pace off the bench often caused problems for teams who were chasing the game. None of Arteta’s remaining options possess that commodity, though Tzolis showed before a difficult half at Villa that he has the ability to create and score goals.

Eze, who missed in the shootout that decided the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain after coming off the bench, replaced the Greece forward against Villa and played a key role in Saka’s winner. Even after his heroics against Tottenham last season, scoring five goals against the team who were gazumped for his signature, the England forward has not nailed down a starting spot in the most important games. Eze could end up being the biggest beneficiary of Arsenal’s transfer inactivity along with Max Dowman, the 16-year-old who has yet to make an appearance this season.

After a summer of transition among their rivals, Arteta is banking on continuity to stay ahead of the pack.

Sports.title: Loan stars: Premier League youngsters to watch in the EFL
Sports.content:
Ollie Whatmuff, Manchester City to Stockport

Goalkeepers are supposed to peak at about 30, which makes one wonder how good the 18-year-old Whatmuff will be at that point. He spent last season playing professionally, earning promotion from the National League with Rochdale under the tutelage of Jimmy McNulty. When the manager jumped two divisions to Stockport, Whatmuff was the first person he wanted to take with him. City showed how highly they think of Whatmuff by incorporating him within their pre-season tour travelling party, where he worked closely with Gianluigi Donnarumma. Whatmuff is extremely composed with the ball at his feet, unfazed by pressure and his surroundings. Those who have worked with him are confident he will spend his career in the Premier League and win full international honours.

Samuel Iling-Junior, Aston Villa to Bolton

The winger has spent his career flitting between England and Italy, taking in Juventus, Middlesbrough, West Brom and Pisa along the way. It feels like a fascinating career but one that needs a more permanent setting. Wingers who can use both feet are incredibly desirable and Iling-Junior is further aided by his pace. Wherever he has been, the 22-year-old has never made his mark consistently but he has the qualities to succeed and requires more game time to hone the skills that enabled him to score in Serie A and earn 16 England Under-21 caps.

View image in fullscreen Bolton’s Samuel Iling-Junior takes on Sheffield United’s Romelle Donovan (left) and Rhys Norrington-Davies (right). Photograph: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock

Charlie Gray, Manchester City to Wigan

Pep Guardiola gave the midfielder his City debut, a fine reward for someone who joined aged five and is an FA Youth Cup winner. He made steady progress until 15 when he sustained a fractured spine, then showed admirable courage and desire to return, only to fracture his shins. The holding midfielder, described as “clever and intelligent” by Guardiola, is regarded as happy to sit in front of the defence. This season was viewed as the right time for Gray to progress his development in the third tier. Gray was not used by Gary Caldwell in Wigan’s opening three games, all of which were lost, but started Wednesday’s home victory against MK Dons.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Mason Melia, Tottenham to Lincoln

It cost a League of Ireland record for Tottenham to sign the forward, who made almost 100 first-team appearances for St Patrick’s Athletic before leaving as an 18-year-old in January. Clubs from across the pyramid and around Europe were interested in Melia, whose clever movement is a key part of his game. He is able to play as the focal point of the attack but can also drop deep and get on the ball. A natural finisher, he will be pushing for more chances at Lincoln, who managed one shot on goal from 18 attempts in their goalless draw with Blackburn on Tuesday.

View image in fullscreen Mason Melia is unveiled at Lincoln. Photograph: Chris Vaughan/Getty Images

Lamin Sillah, Nottingham Forest to Gillingham

The striker, spotted in the Gambia playing for Steve Biko FC, has ticked off time with Olympiakos and Forest. It will be interesting to see how the speedy forward adapts at a club who have scored twice in their opening four matches. Silleh’s ceiling is above the fourth tier but he needs some polishing and that begins with facing League Two defenders on a weekly basis, learning the tricks of the trade from gnarled centre-backs who do not take kindly to Premier League kids

Tommi O’Reilly, Aston Villa to Doncaster

This is a fifth loan for the midfielder, whose journey has taken in the Basque County and Crewe with a few stops in between. It was at Gresty Road last season that he found his feet, playing every game in League Two and scoring seven goals. During his academy days, teammates would compare him to Phil Foden thanks to his skill and style. Grant McCann spent a long time developing young talent at Peterborough and is doing the same at Doncaster, where O’Reilly is aiming to keep his career on an upward trajectory.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Keyrol Figueroa, Liverpool to Port Vale

It would be great to come up with plenty of reasons to follow the striker’s progress from in-depth scouting to being tipped the wink by a Liverpool coach but, ultimately, everyone just wants to see how the son of the former Wigan full-back Maynor Figueroa gets on in League Two. Maynor was a cult hero at the Latics and is still turning out for Whythenshawe Vets. Keyrol spent his youth career playing for USA, the country of his birth, but earned his first Honduras cap this year. He will need a further 180 to match his dad.

Rio Cardines, Crystal Palace to Bristol City

The full-back’s first two Palace games were against Dynamo Kyiv and Arsenal and he has 11 Trinidad & Tobago caps but this season his ability will be consistently challenged. The early signs are good for an athletic, speedy defender eager to get up and down. Versatility made him an attractive option for the Robins, where Michael Skubala is using Cardines at left-back despite the 20-year-old spending more of his career on the right. The change is working because Cardines has made three assists.

View image in fullscreen Rio Cardines of Bristol City (right) in action against Patrick Roberts of Birmingham. Photograph: Ryan Crockett/PA

Harry Howell, Brighton to Leicester

Howell’s selection for a Premier League bench at 16 shows what Brighton think of the attacking midfielder but he had to wait until he turned 17 for his debut against the then champions Liverpool. A cultured player who rolls down his socks, Howell can play in numerous roles in the final third. He was awarded a three-year deal before being sent to Leicester to join the Russell Martin evolution, which includes two more Brighton loanees, Tommy Watson and Kamari Doyle. Howell’s father, Jamie, was a professional who started his career at Arsenal and his cousin Jack Hinshelwood has become a Brighton regular.

Sports.title: Premier League paradox: midfielders are more and more expensive, yet more and more mediocre | Jonathan Liew
Sports.content:
Perhaps the only thing you really need to know about the modern midfield role is that Enzo Maresca reckons that Marc Guéhi can play it better than Mateo Kovacic. Guéhi, in reality a centre-back, started the season in midfield for Manchester City, ahead of Kovacic, the now-departed Nico González, and Matheus Nunes. In this context City’s purchase of Enzo Fernández for a club record £125m can be seen in one of two ways: either an enormous statement of intent, or a hell of a lot of money to pay for Guéhi’s understudy.

We jest, of course. Fernández is in fact a very different kind of midfielder to Guéhi, largely on the basis that he actually is a midfielder. Versatile, able to receive deep from the goalkeeper or the centre-halves; capable of recycling or progressing the ball in tight spots, driving into final-third positions as a No 8, ghosting into the penalty area and offering an advanced goal threat. Like Elliot Anderson, signed from Nottingham Forest for £116m but so long ago that in transfer window time it no longer counts, Fernández is one of the new breed of Premier League central midfielders who seems to offer everything; albeit in modest qualities, and whose primary attribute appears to be the absence of exposed risk he represents.

This is the only real way of explaining the vastly inflated fee City have paid Chelsea in a race where they were the only realistic bidder. Angelo Stiller at Stuttgart – to pluck one name out of the ether – is a similar profile of midfielder of the same age who would probably have been available at half the price, and with exactly one fewer video in which he was filmed making racist and homophobic slurs. But unlike Stiller, Fernández is battle-hardened, Premier League-proven, a known known. Whatever flaws he possesses – from his slow recovery speed to occasional fits of petulance to his intolerance – have been priced in.

And if there is any coherent theme to the 2026 summer window, the Premier League’s surge-pricing era, this is probably it: the Barclays tax, the overwhelming premium applied to players who are adjusted to the league, who have been there, done that and taken the tactical yellow card. Manchester United have added Andrey Santos, Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans in an otherwise quiet summer. Tottenham have maxed out the credit card to bring in Sandro Tonali (£92.5m,) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m). In which context Arsenal’s purchase of Bruno Guimarães for £75m feels like a kind of weird bargain, the £4.50 pack of special offer supermarket butter.

Nevertheless, these are sums that in almost any other Premier League summer would have drawn audible gasps, that would at the very least have been attached to proven superstars, unicorn players, missing pieces of the jigsaw. With the greatest of respect, do any of the midfielders signed by Premier League clubs this summer strike you as that level of player? Anybody who might realistically hold a candle to your Vieiras and Keanes, your Lampard and Gerrards, your De Bruynes and Kantés? Perhaps the underpinning irony of this summer is that the most expensive generation of central midfielders in Premier League history is also – in relative terms – one of its most mediocre.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca chose to play Marc Guéhi in central midfield rather than any of the midfielders he had available. Photograph: Conor Molloy/ProSports/Shutterstock

By way of proof, compile your own list of the best central midfielders operating in world football and count up how many of them are playing in this country. With a few exceptions, the best are elsewhere: Vitinha and João Neves at Paris Saint-Germain, Jude Bellingham at Real Madrid, Pedri and Rodri at Barcelona, Joshua Kimmich at Bayern Munich. Equally you may chuck in Frenkie de Jong, Fabián Ruiz, Fede Valverde, Aurélien Tchouaméni, Warren Zaïre-Emery.

In Premier League terms you have Declan Rice, Moisés Caicedo, Bruno Fernandes and maybe a couple of others. Enzo is handy, Mateus has promise, Baleba has played very well for very short periods of time. But for a league that is by far the world’s richest and most alluring, the absence of generational midfield talents – and particularly creative talents – is not simply an anomaly but a bug that may be progressing into a sickness.

Maresca’s deployment of Guéhi, while also a kind of unsubtle message to the City board, encapsulates this. “This is a country, a league, where you need strong midfielders,” he said, and by strong he meant physical, tenacious, good in duels, good with the shoulders and elbows. Great athletes. Capable of covering every blade of grass. The kind of thing Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Kevin De Bruyne, all in their 30s and pensioned off to slower leagues, can no longer do. A league in which running and duelling has become more important than passing, in which Dominik Szoboszlai has become Liverpool’s most important player more on his ability to get places than his ability to do anything once he gets there.

But while overt physicality is one element of the equation, it is by no means the only one. For football executives answerable to capricious owners and sensitive to public opinion, familiar players offer a kind of cherished security. Signing a known player for big money carries less reputational risk. When Arsenal blow £72m on Nicolas Pépé and it doesn’t work out, that’s Arsenal’s fault. When City blow £100m on Jack Grealish and it doesn’t work out, somehow that’s Grealish’s fault. So it will be with Anderson or Fernández or Morgan Rogers, none of whom are remotely proven, but who are at least responsible for their own failure, which in boardroom terms may as well be the same thing.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This is how you end up with a league as a kind of feedback loop, an arms race in which the aim is not simply to sign the most suitable player for an appropriate sum of money but to ride the waves of the market, a place where inefficiency and overspending are treasured as signs of ambition. And in practice the market will reward you for this: Chelsea sign Alejandro Garnacho, he does nothing, and you potentially sell him on to Aston Villa at a small profit. What possible disincentive is there to keep doing this for as long as you can?

View image in fullscreen Sandro Tonali is a major part of Tottenham’s rebuild, signing from Newcastle in a club record £100m deal. Photograph: Tiego Grenho/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

At times it feels as if the Premier League has been reimagined as a kind of player trading vehicle, a transfer show with 380 football games inconveniently attached. But of course sport does often find a way. World Cup fatigue is yet to set in. Playing a high-energy pressing game in four or five competitions will quickly become an impossibility. According to New York Times data the Premier League still features more intensive sprinting than other “big five” leagues, but here the trend is down while elsewhere it is up. Perhaps this is the season where cohesion, craft, coaching and creativity make their long-awaited comeback?

I once interviewed a youth coach with a longstanding record of producing Premier League players, who lamented to me that academies had begun to neglect technical skill in favour of producing “800-metre runners”. And increasingly this feels like a kind of pivotal season for English football, a test of identities and values, a measure of what it ultimately wants to be. The fastest and the most furious, or the best and most beautiful? If Marc Guéhi ends up going for £150m when the window opens again, we’ll have our answer.

Sports.title: Arsenal poised to land PSG’s Élisa De Almeida on WSL transfer deadline day
Sports.content:
Arsenal are expected to finalise the signing of the France defender Élisa De Almeida before the 11pm BST Women’s Super League transfer deadline. The club are understood to have agreed a fee of just over £500,000 with Paris Saint-Germain for the 28-year-old.

PSG, for whom De Almeida has played since 2021, are less willing to let their Nigeria midfielder Jennifer Echegini go. The 25-year-old is understood to be the subject of interest from Manchester City but PSG were fighting hard to keep her on Thursday morning.

The WSL champions’ desire to add to their squad is understood to have been fuelled partly by the knee injury sustained by Vivianne Miedema, which will keep her out for an unspecified time.

De Almeida is an experienced centre-back who was part of France’s Euro 2025 and 2023 World Cup squads. Arsenal are understood to need centre-back cover partly because their defender Katie Reid’s recovery from the anterior cruciate ligament injury sustained last November is being managed carefully, meaning the 19-year-old is not expected to be available before November.

The WSL season gets under way on Friday when London City Lionesses host Manchester United. The new United head coach, Eva Olid, said on Thursday her team would not add more signings. United secured the Mexico midfielder Rebeca Bernal, who can also play at centre-back, on Wednesday, and Olid said at her first press conference since replacing Marc Skinner that Bernal would be available for Friday’s match.

Olid, the former Hearts manager, is promising to bring “attacking football” to United. She used the word “attacking” eight times during her 17-minute press conference and spoke of her enthusiasm for developing young players. She said of her attacking style: “They appointed me for that reason. I have to go with that. We will be brave in attack, trying to play that attractive football. Our main focus [is] that attacking mentality. We want to play with the ball, a nice football, create a lot of chances.”

On waiting until January before adding more players, Olid said: “The players I need are different from the players the previous manager needed. [It has been a] short period to react. We have some plans in January about signing players that I really need for my style of play. It was not about signing players quick. It is about signing the right players.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Olid was also asked about United’s investment in the women’s game, with Chelsea spending nearly three times as much as them on their women’s team wage bill in the most recent set of published accounts. Olid spoke positively about her club’s backing, saying: “The message has always been about: ‘We want to invest in everything.’ As I said, not just on players. Because I think it is important we have the right staff, the right coaches … The message is that they want to win. They want to win. I think I am here to make that happen, but with a solid identity.”

Sports.title: Azeez to Andrés: seven smart-looking Premier League deadline day deals
Sports.content:
Femi Azeez, Millwall to Brighton, £15m

A tricky, exciting, quick and versatile midfielder, Azeez has proven himself in the Championship with Millwall over the past two seasons and now deserves a chance to test himself in the top flight.

Brighton had been chasing him for a while and struck a deal on deadline day for a very reasonable reported initial £12.5m, rising to £15m. If he can make the step up and produce anything like his second-tier form, he’ll be a steal.

He is a high-volume producer at the sharp end of the pitch, constantly making things happen that threaten the opposition’s goal, but standing out most for his crossing. He ranked top of the Championship last season for open-play crosses (227) and expected assists from crosses (6.71 xA).

He also ranked fourth for dribble attempts (131), ninth for shots (95), sixth for chances created from open play (58). He created good-quality chances, too; only two players created more big chances than he did (18), and he ranked fourth for expected assists. His 9.12 xA alongside only seven assists suggests he may benefit from playing alongside better finishers.

View image in fullscreen Femi Azeez’s expected assists. Photograph: Opta

Ibrahim Mbaye, PSG to Aston Villa, £47m

A hugely exciting prospect. Despite being 18, Mbaye has significant and noteworthy experience under his belt. Last year he made six appearances, including in the final, for Senegal at the Africa Cup of Nations and this summer he made four appearances at the World Cup. He has also played in two Ligue 1 title-winning campaigns, including 2024-25, when he became the youngest player in PSG’s history to start a game, and won the Champions League in both of those seasons

He is a dribbling and ball-carrying menace, who always looks as if he’s about to do something special. Among players to play at least 900 minutes in Ligue 1 last season, he was 11th for carries (moving at least five metres with the ball) per 90, with 20.0, and 12th for progressive carries (moving at least five metres upfield with the ball) per 90, with 10.3. Most of the players above him in both lists are defenders, who naturally have more space to move into.

He was third for take-on-ending carries, or running with the ball for at least five metres before attempting to beat an opponent with a dribble, with 2.9 per 90. And he also has end product to boot. He scored at Afcon and the World Cup despite limited minutes and his 0.45 goals or assists per 90 for PSG last season is not to be sniffed at.

Kevin Danso, Spurs to Sunderland, loan with buy obligation

Danso had a pretty impossible task over his two years at Tottenham. He was the back-up to the first-choice centre-backs Cristian Romero and Micky van de Ven, playing intermittently on both sides of central defence in dysfunctional teams jumping between styles of play, and he very rarely played for any consistent run of games.

He was unfairly compared with the players he was replacing for much of his time there, but the truth is he was always reliable enough. He excelled, however, when Romero got injured during the run-in last season and he was called upon in Spurs’ time of need as they scraped clear of relegation.

He may not be the best on the ball – though he is hardly terrible – but he is an excellent deep defender. Among those to play at least 1,000 minutes in the Premier League last season, Danso ranked first for clearances (8.2 per 90) and headed clearances (6.3), and was fifth for aerial duels won (4.8 per 90).

He could thrive at Sunderland, who spent more of their out-of-possession game time in a low block than any other team in the Premier League last season (25%). Danso could be perfectly at home in this setup, paired alongside the player he beat into second place for clearances and headed clearances: Dan Ballard.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland’s low-block, time used. Photograph: Opta

Iliman Ndiaye, Everton to Man City, £65m

It was always said during Pep Guardiola’s time at Manchester City that attackers had their wings clipped in terms of individual freedom, limited to playing within the parameters of the manager’s meticulous gameplan.

But dribbling ability became increasingly important in the final years of his reign, with Jérémy Doku and Antoine Semenyo on the wings and Rayan Cherki in between. Doku (162) and Semenyo (144) ranked first and second for dribbles attempted in the Premier League last season, with Cherki ninth (111). They also ranked first (84), fourth (59) and eighth (51), respectively, for dribbles completed.

With the deadline-day addition of Ndiaye, City have gone in even harder on dribbling ability under Enzo Maresca. The Senegal international ranked second for dribbles attempted (136) and dribbles completed (73) in the Premier League last season.

View image in fullscreen Iliman Ndiaye’s dribbles. Photograph: Opta

Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Lille to Newcastle, £51m

Fernandez-Pardo’s versatility is a major attraction. He’s comfortable playing off the left and cutting in on to his right foot, or as a No 9. Although not the bulkiest, he has explosive pace and promises to be a threat in behind.

The Belgium international is arguably at his most threatening when running with the ball because he does so with such purpose. His 122 carries progressing the ball at least 10 metres upfield in Ligue 1 last term were bettered by only seven players, several of whom were defenders.

On top of that, he ranked top for carries into the penalty area (69) and seventh for carries ending with a shot or chance created (39).

View image in fullscreen Matias Fernandez-Pardo’s chance creating carries. Photograph: Opta

Malick Fofana, Lyon to Sunderland, £30m

Fofana appeared to be enjoying a swift rise in 2024-25, only for a serious ankle injury to massively disrupt his development in 2025-26. Sunderland will be hoping they can get him back to the levels shown the season before last, when he was a real livewire on Lyon’s left flank.

He contributed nine goal involvements (five goals, four assists) in 1,586 minutes in Ligue 1 in 2024-25, averaging one every 176 minutes. Only eight forwards (900+ mins) averaged more expected assists per 90 (0.25).

The most eye-catching aspects of his game, however, were his dynamism and pace. He could be difficult to stop once moving, and this made him a very useful outlet. Among Ligue 1 forwards (900+ mins), his 16.6 carries per 90 ranked him sixth, and he moved up to third for progressive carries per 90 (11.5).

Fofana is direct, exciting and has significant potential. He is a player Sunderland could make a profit on if he reaches the levels previously expected.

Chema Andrés, Stuttgart to Brighton, £20m

Andrés arrived to bolster Brighton’s midfield options after Carlos Baleba’s exit to Manchester United. Although a different type of midfielder to the Cameroonian, Chema is another with vast potential.

A product of Real Madrid’s academy, Chema joined Stuttgart last summer. During his sole campaign in the Bundesliga, he was in and out of the team but caught the eye at the base of their midfield.

Comparisons have been made to Rodri because of his physical attributes and nominal role as a holding midfielder. He doesn’t have anything like the same influence in possession but Chema is tidy on the ball.

It’s what he offers defensively that is most notable, however. He’s been broadly praised for his anticipation and reading of the game, ranking second among midfielders (900+ mins) since the start of last season for interceptions per 90 in the Bundesliga (2.3).

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Two Arsenal players missing from training days before huge Chelsea showdown
Sports.content:
Bruno Guimaraes and Cristhian Mosquera both missed Arsenal training three days before Sunday's home London derby against Chelsea.

Arsenal had an open training session on Thursday morning, but Guimaraes and Mosquera were not involved.



2 Guimaraes played his first 19 Premier League minutes for Arsenal last time out Credit: Getty

Good news and bad news for Arsenal

Both players featured in Monday's 1-0 win at Aston Villa, with Guimaraes making his Premier League debut for the Gunners from the bench following a short spell on the sidelines.

Mosquera started the game but was forced off towards the end of the second half by a muscular problem.

It remains to be seen whether either will be available for the visit of Chelsea, where both sides put their 100 per cent starts to the season on the line.



Guimaraes had started last month's Community Shield victory over Manchester City but missed Arsenal's Premier League opener against Coventry with a minor groin issue.

The Brazil midfielder was Arsenal's most expensive signing of the summer transfer window, joining from Newcastle for £75m.



Mosquera had been covering for the injured William Saliba, though the Gunners have also signed Ezri Konsa – who replaced Mosquera for the final 10 minutes against Villa, the club he'd just arrived from.

Konsa could be in line to make his first Arsenal start this weekend, then.



Saliba is expected to be out until at least the middle of October with a back injury.

More positively on the injury front for Mikel Arteta, Declan Rice has been training after hobbling off late on in the Villa game.

Jurrien Timber has also been back training solo after missing the Netherlands' World Cup campaign through a groin injury.

2 Mosquera has started all three games in all competitions for the Gunners this term Credit: Getty



The Gunners' perfect start

Arsenal have begun their Premier League title defence in ideal fashion, kicking off by beating Coventry 3-0 before picking up three more points and keeping another clean sheet last time out.

But Chelsea are set to present their sternest test of the campaign so far.

Xabi Alonso's Blues are the joint top-scoring side in the Premier League so far with seven goals – and while they've also conceded six goals themselves, they have successfully seen off Fulham 3-2 and Brighton 4-3.

Arsenal, though, have an excellent recent record at the Emirates Stadium against their London rivals.



Chelsea haven't won there since August 2021, with the Gunners coming out on top in each of the last five meetings in all competitions in north London.

Chelsea team news

The Blues have a number of injury worries of their own: Jordan Henderson remains sidelined after breaking his arm in a freak incident at the World Cup, while fellow summer signing Marco Palestra – also yet to make his debut – is still doubtful.

Alonso will also be hoping the issue that forced Moises Caicedo off against Brighton is not serious, as he initially thought.

Sports.title: Nine big-name players out of contract next summer from Harry Kane to Bruno Fernandes and two Liverpool stars
Sports.content:
Nine big-name players out of contract next summer from Harry Kane to Bruno Fernandes and two Liverpool stars

The summer transfer window may have just closed, but that does not stop the rumour mill churning.

One of the big talking points at the end of every season is the high-profile names who are out of contract and therefore have freedom of choice over their next destination.

9 Silva joined Real Madrid this summer in a blockbuster free transfer Credit: Getty

This summer we have seen the likes of Bernardo Silva join Real Madrid and John Stones head to Inter Milan. Meanwhile, people like Jadon Sancho are still without a club.

Those who are available in July 2027 for nothing will already be on the radar of clubs around Europe and beyond.

From January, those players can enter negotiations with clubs outside their current league and sign pre-contract agreements, should they wish to.

And there are some superstars who, currently, have their contracts expiring next summer.

talkSPORT.com has taken a look at the nine biggest names with less than a year left on their deals.

Harry Kane

The England captain is, as things stand, going to become a free agent next summer.

If this were to come to pass then it would create pandemonium around Europe. He is arguably the best player in the world right now and a favourite for the Ballon d’Or.

In all likelihood, the 33-year-old will sign a new contract extension with Bayern Munich, talks have started.

But if those break down then it could put plenty of teams on high alert. One sticking point appears to be the length of the deal.

Kane said: "The first meeting was this week. But such matters are not settled in a week or two. There will be many other discussions about the details."

9 Kane has scored 148 goals in 150 games for Bayern Credit: Getty

Asked about the contract clauses, the England captain added: "I won't talk about the details here."

Things are going well, so everything is fine so far. We will continue the dialogue in the coming weeks and see what happens."

Kane added: "There are many factors that affect a contract like this: I am 33 years old, so this may not be my last contract, but it is certainly an important contract for me. I need to be happy, and the club also needs to be happy.

“The good thing is that both parties are not worried. At the moment, they are just open discussions, as is the case with any contract in my career."

Bruno Fernandes

Fernandes remains Manchester United’s best player and has been for some time.

The 31-year-old is at the peak of his powers and showed that with a hat-trick against Ipswich on Sunday.

9 Fernandes is the reigning PFA Player of the Year Credit: Getty

United were prepared to sell him last summer when Al Nassr came in with an £80m bid. Ruben Amorim was said to have blocked his exit.

The Red Devils are keen to get Fernandes to sign a contract extension to make him the best paid player at the club.

He currently earns around £300,000-a-week, but that could increase by another £50,000.

The reigning PFA Player of the Year has also been named Manchester United’s best player in five of his seven seasons at the club.

Lisandro Martinez

World Cup winner Martinez is facing a fight to save his Manchester United career.

As reported in the talkSPORT Notebook, sources have confirmed the club are ready to take up the extra year’s option in Martinez’s contract, which is due to expire at the end of the season.

9 Martinez joined Man United from Ajax in 2022 Credit: Getty

However, there is a feeling inside the corridors of power at Carrington that the Argentine needs to prove his ability to stay fit or be sold next summer.

Since joining United from Ajax four years ago, Martinez - affectionately known as ‘The Butcher’ by fans - has missed almost 80 Premier League games due to various injuries. He also turns 29 in January.

If United decide against activating that extra year option, however unlikely, then the 28-year-old would be free to walk away.

Christian Pulisic

USMNT star Pulisic is entering the final 12 months of his contract with AC Milan, who do still hold an option of extending that for another year.

Reports emerged earlier this summer that Major League Soccer (MLS) club New York City FC were looking to make a move for the forward, offering a salary of $11.3 million per season over a five-year contract.

AC Milan were not entertaining the idea of selling him this summer, but his future is sure to be a hot topic of discussion come July.

9 Pulisic left Chelsea in 2023 for AC Milan Credit: Getty

Brahim Diaz

The 27-year-old is now in the final 12 months of his contract at Real Madrid.

There has long been talk over negotiations to extend his deal until 2030, but as yet there has been no sign of an official announcement.

Should these talks break down or not happen, then he would be available on a free transfer next summer.

The Morocco World Cup star has started one game this season for Madrid, but will find increasing competition for a place following the signing of Yan Diomande.

9 Diaz started his career at Man City before joining Real Madrid in 2019 Credit: Getty

Alisson

Liverpool triggered Alisson Becker’s one-year contract extension last season to keep him at the club until 2027.

The likelihood is the 33-year-old will leave Anfield after an illustrious nine seasons, where he has won two Premier League titles and the Champions League.

Liverpool already have Giorgi Mamardashvili as his back-up and recently signed 18-year-old Lucca Brughmans from Genk, where he has returned on loan for the 2026/27 campaign.

9 Alisson has played 335 games for Liverpool Credit: Getty

Virgil van Dijk

Van Dijk is another Liverpool stalwart expected to end his time at Anfield at the end of the season.

He penned a two-year extension in April 2025, taking him until the summer of 2027.

There are no signs that it will be increased further for the 35-year-old club captain.

Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni are expected to be his long-term replacements.

9 Van Dijk was worth every penny of the £75m Liverpool paid Southampton in 2018 Credit: Getty

Kaoru Mitoma

The 29-year-old has been a revelation in the Premier League since joining Brighton from Kawasaki Frontale in 2021.

The Japan star was denied a trip to the World Cup this summer after suffering a hamstring injury during a Premier League game in May.

His contract will expire at the end of the season, with the dynamic winger expected to be hugely in demand should he be available on a free transfer.

Tyrick Mitchell

Mitchell has been the model of consistency at Crystal Palace over a number of seasons, flourishing under Oliver Glasner.

He helped Palace win the FA Cup, Community Shield, and Conference League.

The 27-year-old has perhaps been unlucky to be constantly overlooked for a place in the England squad.

The Palace academy graduate has played 246 times since making his debut in the 2019/20 campaign.

There will likely be plenty of interest should he not extend his stay at Selhurst Park beyond the end of the season.

Sports.title: Sunderland star in talks over late transfer exit amid Europa League squad snub
Sports.content:
Chemsdine Talbi has been left out of Sunderland's Europa League squad as talks continue over a potential move.

The Black Cats have submitted their 22-man squad for the continental competition following a hectic summer.

2 Talbi is likely to leave Sunderland in the coming days Credit: Getty

The 21-year-old has featured sporadically for the north-east outfit, and was benched in the 1-0 win over Fulham last weekend.

talkSPORT understands the Morocco international has been in talks with Saudi Pro League club Al-Ittihad.

Turkish Super Lig clubs Galatasaray and Fenerbahce are also interested in the winger.

Because the transfer windows in Saudi Arabia and Turkey remain open, Talbi can still seal a move away from Wearside despite the Premier League deadline having passed.

The youngster only signed for the club from Club Brugges for £18million last summer.

Speaking in a press conference on Thursday, Sunderland manager Regis Le Bris said: "A move remains possible so it's important to respect both parties. We'll see.

"He's still a good player, huge potential but after that you still have a window to decide if it's the right pathway here.

"I believe he can succeed here, but after that it's a question of mutual confidence and you have to respect the player's choice."

Who is in Sunderland's Europa League squad?

Robin Roefs and Simon Moore are the named goalkeepers in the Europa League squad.

The nine defenders are Omar Alderete, Dan Ballard, Kevin Danso, Trai Hume, Reinildo, Dayann Méthalie, Thomas Meunier, Nordi Mukiele and Luke O'Nien.

2 Talbi became a crucial player at times for Sunderland last season Credit: AFP

Midfield options are Jules Ahoka, Habib Diarra, Enzo Le Fee, Chris Rigg, Noah Sadiki and Granit Xhaka.

The forwards are Nilson Angulo, Brian Brobbey, Malick Fofana, Wilson Isidor and Romaine Mundle.

Eligible youngsters can still be registered on List B during the league phase; but Talbi does not meet those requirements.

He is young enough to meet the age requirement for List B, but he cannot be registered through that route because he has not been at Sunderland for the required two-year period.

The Morocco international netted four times in 28 Premier League games during his first season in the English top-flight.

After the campaign, Talbi was selected in Morocco's 26-man squad for the World Cup in North America.

Sports.title: Mike Dean criticised after viral clip admitting to ‘playing games’ while refereeing
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League referee Mike Dean has been criticised for admitting he played 'mini-games' while officiating.

Dean became arguably the most recognised official in English football after taking charge of 553 top-flight matches over a 22-year career.



2 Dean retired as a video assistant referee (VAR) official in 2023. Credit: Getty

He was often labelled by fans as 'arrogant' and made a name for himself as one of the biggest personalities in refereeing.

The 58-year-old hung up his whistle following the 2021/22 campaign and became a VAR official.

Since retiring from the game completely, Dean has launched a media career, offering his insights on the game as a former referee.



He recently went viral during an appearance on Jamie Vardy's new podcast.

Dean said: "There used to be games that we used to have, as a laugh, we used to say, 'Right, we'll kick off now, right? See how long we can go without blowing a whistle.



"Done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR obviously. Went 20–25 minutes without blowing the whistle a few times. Let it go, let it go, let it go.

"I used to do another thing in the Premier League. I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about.



"I used to do another thing in the Premier League. I used to stand in the centre circle and see how long I could stay in the centre circle before I had to leave. That was just me joking about."

It has sparked a backlash among fans, with ProRef deciding to make no comment when approached.

talkSPORT's Gabby Agbonlahor, who played for Aston Villa during Dean's career, was left furious by the revelation.

2 Dean was at the centre of many huge Premier League moments during his career Credit: Getty



He said: "I didn't get on with Mike Dean at all. He's the sort of referee that gives it back to players.

"He had that arrogance about him. One word to describe him. I would say he's a prat. That's just the perfect word for him.

"I just think back to games now and I'm like, you were refereeing games and you were having a joke about.

"It’s like, ‘Oh okay, I want to beat my friend who I've had a little joke with. How long can we go without blowing our whistle or leaving the centre circle?,



"Referees should be up and down so they don't miss anything, there was no VAR back then.

"So you might have missed penalties or free kicks because you want to joke and stay in the centre circle."

It is not the first time that Dean has prompted controversy when speaking about his career.

The ex-official has previously admitted not referring a decision to VAR, in an attempt to protect a friend.



During a fiery draw between Chelsea and Tottenham in August 2022 and claimed he avoided sending Anthony Taylor to the screen to review a missed hair pull on Marc Cucurella as his colleague had endured a tough match.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes would not start for every Premier League team, one No.10 is better
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes would not start for every Premier League team, one No.10 is better

Jason Cundy believes there is one Premier League team Bruno Fernandes does not get in.

The talkSPORT host was discussing the merits of the Manchester United captain, who was named Player of the Year last season with co-host Jamie O'Hara on The Sports Bar.



3 Fernandes gets into every Premier League team, except one, says Cundy Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Having listened to Weekend Sport Breakfast Tony Cascarino explain he can't see a world right now where Fernandes is a first team selection in Chelsea's current star-studded attack, Cundy believes he is not the best no.10 in the league right now.

Is Fernandes the Premier League's best No.10?

He enjoyed a stellar campaign last season, setting a new Premier League assists record with 21 as Manchester United qualified for the Champions League.

Meanwhile, Fernandes was also named the FWA Footballer of the Year, Premier League Player of the Season and PFA Players' Player of the year.



"I don’t think he’d be in the Chelsea team, with what Chelsea have now," Cascarino said. "Would I take Morgan Rogers [out], I’m going Cole Palmer and I’m going [Joao Pedro] down the middle?

"Unless you change your system. You might play him as a 10, which you can do a bit deeper then, absolutely, he’d make the team."



Who is better than Fernandes?

O'Hara was unconvinced by the argument, though, declaring Fernandes is the best in the league in his position, whilst Cundy said he preferred Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard, who won the Premier League last season.

"Over the last four or five seasons [Odegaard has been the best] because, in my opinion, four years ago Odegaard was the best No.10 in the country.



"Bruno then wasn’t doing what he did last season."

3 Cundy believes Odegaard is better than Fernandes and would keep him out of the Arsenal team Credit: Getty

O'Hara responded, telling Cundy: "Bruno doesn’t get the credit he deserves."

Stunned by the claim, his co-host exclaimed: "What do you mean? He won PFA Player of the Year. That's getting credit.

"You can't pretend that's not getting credit. (Has Fernandes been better) over the last 12 months? Yes, that's undeniable."



As for Fernandes' performance on the opening weekend against Hull City, Cundy added: "How was he against Hull? Have you forgotten about that?

"Have you erased that from your memory? He was absolutely dog poop."

It was not just O'Hara and Cundy who gave their stance on the debate, though, with United fan Spencer calling the show.

Arguing his case, he said: "Fernandes would get in every team in the league, no doubt about it.

"Arsenal would have already won a lot of league titles if he'd gone there when he came to United. Simple as that.



3

"I think he's one of the best players that the league has had in a long time and I definitely think he would have got in any Sir Alex Ferguson team in any era."

Odegaard and Fernandes compared

Fernandes followed up United's defeat to Hull with a hat-trick and an assist in a 5-2 win over Ipswich on Sunday, though.

Since joining the Red Devils in January 2020, Fernandes has amassed 74 goals and 73 assists in 232 Premier League outings.



He will be hoping to add to that tally away at Everton on Sunday, with kick-off at 2pm.

In contrast to Fernandes' output, Odegaard has 36 goals and 37 assists in 178 Premier League appearances for Arsenal.

However, the Gunners captain often operates in a deeper midfield role and guided the club to their first league title for 22 years last term.

After an initial loan spell from Real Madrid, Odegaard joined Arsenal permanently in the summer of 2021.

Sports.title: Hugh Jackman reveals talks over buying stake in Championship club he supported since age of seven
Sports.content:
Hollywood superstar Hugh Jackman is in talks to buy a stake in Norwich City, talkSPORT has been told.

Jackman is a boyhood Canaries fan and his UK-born mother comes from Norwich.

4 Jackman is one of the most famous actors in the world Credit: Getty

The Wolverine star is also close friends with Ryan Reynolds, who famously co-owns Norwich's Championship rivals Wrexham alongside fellow actor Rob Mac.

When asked whether he could join the Hollywood revolution in English football, Jackman told talkSPORT: "I'm very, very interested - and talking about it right now.

"You're the first one to know that. There's a little exclusive.

"Good on Ryan, you do your thing, I'm all about the Canaries."

Jackman did not specify how much of Norwich he was interested in purchasing.

The Australian was invited to become a minority investor in 2010, but turned it down.

Speaking in 2011, Jackman said: "Sometimes I make big mistakes.

"I got a letter about a year ago saying, being such a huge Norwich City fan would I like to be a celebrity investor? Like a small part-owner.

"I said, 'I think that's a little stretched, I've been to Carrow Road once, my mum took me', so I decided not to invest.

"And since then they're on a run, so what do I know?"

4 Jackman and Reynolds could become rivals in the Championship Credit: Getty

Norwich, currently in the second-tier, are majority-owned by American businessman Mark Attanasio, who holds an 85 per cent stake.

He also runs Major League Baseball team Milwaukee Brewers.

Celebrity fans Delia Smith and Michael Wynn-Jones still retain a 10 per cent stake after their 28 years of active leadership ended in 2024.

The remaining five per cent of shares are held by a collection of independent fans and individual investors.

Why does Hugh Jackman support Norwich?

Although the Greatest Showman star was born and raised in Australia, his parents are English.

Jackman, who is said to have a net worth of around £100million, has a connection with Norwich dating back to when he was seven-years old.

4 Norwich are no strangers to celebrity investment - dating back to Smith's cash injection in 1996 Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Speaking at the release of his new film 'The Death of Robin Hood', the 57-year-old added: "When I was in Australia, growing up, I had English parents who emigrated to Australia.

"We used to watch the FA Cup. It was the only thing we were allowed to stay up for, 3 o'clock in the morning. We had to go to bed first, and we were woken up to watch it.

"So I was seeing all these teams, Arsenal and all these teams, and I was like, 'I've got to pick a team'.

"I said, 'Dad, where are you from?' He said, 'London'. I said, 'So I'll go for London?'

"He goes, 'No, there's a bunch of teams in London'. I said, 'Mum, where are you from?' She went, 'Norwich'.

"I went, 'Is there a football team in Norwich?' She went, 'Yep'. I said, 'That's my team'.

4 Norwich are currently 20th in the Championship after three defeats in their opening four games Credit: Getty

"So it's been slim pickings since then. We did win the Milk Cup in 1984.

It's not even called the Milk Cup anymore, but we're on the rise.

"We're on the up and up. I went to Carrow Road a couple of times, and I love the Canaries, and this is the year we're going to get promoted. That's my prediction.

"My prediction is Norwich and Wrexham are getting promoted this year."

English football's Hollywood revolution

Reynolds and Mac's transformation of the Red Dragons has been well-documented, while the Championship also boasts NFL legends Tom Brady and JJ Watt as investors in Birmingham and Burnley respectively.

Elsewhere, hip-hop legend Snoop Dogg recently acquired a minority stake in Swansea alongside Croatia icon Luka Modric.

In the Premier League, music star Ed Sheeran owns 1.4 per cent of boyhood club Ipswich and comedy actor Will Ferrell is an investor in Leeds.

Sports.title: Where to watch Everton vs Manchester United: Man City loanee Grealish eyes start
Sports.content:
Everton entertain Manchester United in an intriguing Premier League encounter this weekend.

The Toffees have taken four points from their opening two games to Man United's three, though the visitors did get their campaign up and running in style with a 5-2 win over Ipswich last time out.



3 Bruno Fernandes hit a hat-trick as Man United thumped Ipswich Credit: Getty

Having beaten Crystal Palace 2-0 at home on the first weekend of the season, Everton maintained their unbeaten start thanks to James Tarkowski's stoppage-time equaliser at Bournemouth in their last outing.

One of the few fixtures that's been played in every Premier League campaign to date, this will be the 174th all-time meeting between Everton and United.

Everton boss David Moyes comes up against the club he left the Toffees to take charge of back in 2013, following Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement.



And for his opposite number, Michael Carrick, it's a repeat of one of his earliest games in charge of United, who he led to a 1-0 victory on Merseyside in February.

Where to watch Everton vs Man United

Everton face United on Sunday, September 6.

Kick-off at Hill Dickinson Stadium is scheduled for 2pm.

Fans will be able to watch the action live on Sky Sports Main Event, Sky Sports Premier League and Sky Sports UHD in the UK.



talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will also keep you up to date with all the latest Premier League news.

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.



Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

3 Marcus Rashford made his first United start since December 2024 last time out Credit: Getty



Everton vs Man United team news

Moyes could have a full squad at his disposal, with Christian Norgaard – yet to make his debut since joining from Arsenal – Everton's only injury doubt.

It's a different story for Man United, with Carrick unable to call on Matthijs de Ligt, Amad and new signing Carlos Baleba – while Manuel Ugarte is set to miss most of the season after suffering a serious knee injury playing for Uruguay at the World Cup.

Mason Mount is also a doubt for the visitors.

While United didn't do any transfer business in the final days of the window, Everton saw notable moves in and out of the club.

Jack Grealish is back on loan from Manchester City and could go straight into the side as the Toffees begin life without Iliman Ndiaye, who headed the other way in a permanent deal.



3 Jack Grealish has returned for a second loan spell at Everton Credit: Getty

Grealish ready to face Man United

Following his loan more from Man City, Grealish is eager to play and could start against United.

He said: "It feels so good. I'm so happy. I think I'm at my best at everything in life, not just football, when I feel loved. That's what the manager has given me, what my teammates have given me and especially what the fans have given me.



"Every time I see an Everton fan, it's just pure love and the way they've welcomed me since that first game against Leeds, I'll never forget that. It means a lot to me and hopefully I've made a few Everton fans happy.

"I had a perfect time here for the first six months, then I stayed around after I got injured. I’ve been watching all the Everton games in pre-season and since the season started.



"Now I feel ready to go. I'm ready to start training tomorrow and prepare for the games."

Meanwhile, Carrick hailed Fernandes following his hat-trick last time out.

He said: "He showed his quality. Bruno did what he's good at. He's had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

"There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it's the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn't go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.



"We're not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn't wrong. We can still get better, we haven't cracked it. We'll get ready for the next."

Sports.title: The incredible story of one of the craziest deadline day sagas EVER: How Malick Fofana joined Sunderland after interest from three clubs, undergoing a medical for TWO sides and changing his mind throughout the day
Sports.content:
Deadline day usually throws up one or two surprises – but not often one like this. The day, for Malick Fofana, started with Arsenal, on the hunt for a left winger, registering their interest. It ended with him signing for Sunderland. And it had plenty in between. The former Lyon man would eventually move to the Black Cats in a deal worth around £30.6million, though changed his mind more than once. It became clear pretty early on on deadline day that Arsenal were going to pull out of a deal due to the price tag, which allowed Sunderland to swoop and agree a deal. Only Crystal Palace smelt blood. Manager Pierre Sage, who had worked with Fofana at Lyon, is believed to have led the charge, and Palace agreed the finances too. Fofana found himself at Lyon airport with two private jets waiting for him – one belonging to Sunderland, and one belonging to Crystal Palace. Malick Fofana endured a sensational deadline day, with Sunderland and Crystal Palace battling it out to sign him Sunderland eventually got their man after Crystal Palace had worked hard to hijack the deal Then, in perhaps the most bizarre part of the story, Fofana underwent a medical for both sides. That took place in Lyon, but both Palace and Sunderland had access. By that point, Black Cats owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus had flown to Lyon to try and personally persuade Fofana to pick his side. Sunderland were also looking at moving for Dodi Lukebakio, but he later opted to stay put at Benfica. Eventually, with a little over an hour to go until the deadline, Fofana chose Sunderland, having changed his mind a number of times, and set off. Sunderland were still forced to submit a deal sheet to get the move over the line, with the transfer announced officially at 12:15am. To wrap it up, the Black Cats captioned his signing video: 'It was always Sunderland.' It, most certainly, was not. HOW FOFANA CHOSE SUNDERLAND 9:10am: Arsenal make interest in potential move known 10:04am: Gunners pull out of a potential move, citing the price tag as the reason why 10:47am: Sunderland agree a deal with Lyon to sign Fofana 1:00pm: Crystal Palace make their move, contacting Fofana directly 3:18pm: Palace agree a deal with Lyon as Sunderland enter negotiations for Dodi Lukebakio 3:40pm: Fofana, undecided on who he wants to join, waits at Lyon airport with private jets headed for Sunderland and south London also present 8:24pm: Sunderland owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus flies to Lyon to try and convince Fofana to pick the Black Cats, before talks over a move for Lukebakio end 9:50pm: Fofana finally picks Sunderland, ending Crystal Palace's hopes of a move 10:54pm: Sunderland submit a deal sheet to get an extension to complete the deal 12:15am: Sunderland finally announce Fofana as their player
